target_user_groups: Researchers in finance and information systems
Entrepreneurs and investors in the DeFi sector
intended_purposes: Systematically structure the emerging field of decentralized finance by classifying DeFi applications
Analyze the DeFi landscape to identify patterns and opportunities for value propositions and business models
Support the design of regulatory measures
input.domain_of_objects: Decentralized finance (DeFi) applications: financial services built on smart contracts on public blockchains without intermediaries

meta_characteristic: The taxonomy views DeFi applications as financial services built on smart contracts on public blockchains that operate without intermediaries, classifying them by how they create and capture value (strategy), how they coordinate participants and governance without central intermediaries (organization), and how their smart contracts and blockchain infrastructure are implemented (technology).

dimensions.name: Primary financial service
dimensions.definition: The main financial function that the DeFi application provides to its users.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign the characteristic that matches the core function the application performs for users; if several functions apply, choose the one that generates the application's main activity. Use the negation when the object is not a financial service.

characteristics.name: Lending and borrowing
characteristics.definition: Users supply assets to, or borrow assets from, the application's markets.

characteristics.name: Trading and exchange
characteristics.definition: Users swap or trade tokens or derivatives against liquidity pools or order books.

characteristics.name: Stablecoin issuance
characteristics.definition: The application issues a stablecoin as its core product.

characteristics.name: Staking and restaking
characteristics.definition: Users stake or restake assets to secure networks or to earn rewards through the application.

characteristics.name: Yield aggregation and management
characteristics.definition: The application allocates user deposits across other DeFi protocols or yield strategies, or trades yield exposure.

characteristics.name: Synthetic asset issuance
characteristics.definition: The application mints synthetic assets that track other assets against collateral.

characteristics.name: Tokenization of real-world assets
characteristics.definition: The application issues tokenized funds, Treasury securities or commodities for on-chain use.

characteristics.name: Insurance cover
characteristics.definition: The application sells cover against smart contract failures.

characteristics.name: Payments
characteristics.definition: The application enables payments in cryptocurrency.

characteristics.name: Cross-chain asset transfer
characteristics.definition: The application moves assets between different blockchains.

characteristics.name: No financial service
characteristics.definition: The object is not a financial service, such as social, identity, storage, naming, gaming or infrastructure applications.

dimensions.name: Stablecoin collateral model
dimensions.definition: How the peg of a stablecoin is backed.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign only to stablecoin objects according to their backing, applying the first matching rule in this order: fiat-reserve backing if the peg is backed by off-chain fiat reserves held by the issuer, even if crypto collateral is also used; synthetic hedged backing if the crypto collateral is hedged with short futures or held in a pooled-debt structure; crypto-collateralized peg if the stablecoin is minted against on-chain crypto collateral without such hedging; algorithmic mint-and-burn peg otherwise when the peg relies on a paired token. Use the negation for objects that are not stablecoins.

characteristics.name: Crypto-collateralized peg
characteristics.definition: The stablecoin is minted against on-chain crypto collateral, overcollateralized or as a basket, without hedging by short futures or a pooled-debt structure.

characteristics.name: Fiat-reserve backing
characteristics.definition: The stablecoin is backed by off-chain fiat reserves held by its issuer.

characteristics.name: Algorithmic mint-and-burn peg
characteristics.definition: The peg is maintained by minting and burning a paired token rather than by reserves.

characteristics.name: Synthetic hedged backing
characteristics.definition: The stablecoin is backed by crypto collateral hedged with short futures or held in a pooled-debt structure.

characteristics.name: Not a stablecoin
characteristics.definition: The object is not a stablecoin.

dimensions.name: Governance mechanism
dimensions.definition: How protocol decisions are taken without a central intermediary.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign by the decision mechanism described: token-holder governance when holders of a governance token decide, including Snapshot votes; member voting when members assess claims. Use the negation when no governance vote is described.

characteristics.name: Token-holder governance
characteristics.definition: Protocol decisions are made by holders of a governance token, including votes run through Snapshot.

characteristics.name: Member voting on claims
characteristics.definition: Members vote to assess claims made against a cover pool.

characteristics.name: No token or member governance
characteristics.definition: No governance vote is described; the rules are fixed in the smart contracts.

dimensions.name: Asset custody model
dimensions.definition: Who holds the assets that users deposit or that back a token.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign non-custodial operation when users keep control of assets through smart contracts without a custodian; assign custodian or issuer when an identified third party holds the underlying or backing assets. Use the negation when the object holds or backs no user assets.

characteristics.name: Non-custodial operation
characteristics.definition: Assets are held by smart contracts or users, without a custodian.

characteristics.name: Custodian or issuer holds assets
characteristics.definition: An identified custodian or issuer holds the underlying or backing assets.

characteristics.name: No user assets involved
characteristics.definition: The object does not hold or back user assets, such as data, identity, social or storage services.

dimensions.name: Blockchain deployment
dimensions.definition: Which public blockchain or blockchains the application runs on.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign multiple public blockchains if the object is deployed on several public blockchains; otherwise assign own layer-1 or sidechain if the object runs its own chain; otherwise assign the single public blockchain it runs on, Ethereum mainnet or another public blockchain. Use the negation when the object does not run on a public blockchain.

characteristics.name: Ethereum mainnet deployment
characteristics.definition: The application runs on the Ethereum blockchain as its only public blockchain.

characteristics.name: Multiple public blockchains
characteristics.definition: The application is deployed on several public blockchains.

characteristics.name: Own layer-1 or sidechain
characteristics.definition: The application runs on its own layer-1 blockchain or on a sidechain it operates.

characteristics.name: Other single public blockchain
characteristics.definition: The application runs on one public blockchain other than Ethereum, such as Solana, BNB Smart Chain or Base.

characteristics.name: No public blockchain deployment
characteristics.definition: The object does not run on a public blockchain.

dimensions.name: Cross-chain message verification
dimensions.definition: How cross-chain transfers or messages are verified.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign only to objects that move assets or messages between blockchains, choosing by the party that verifies them: oracles or independent relayers, or a validator or guardian network that signs messages. Use the negation for objects without a cross-chain function.

characteristics.name: Oracle or relayer verification
characteristics.definition: Cross-chain transfers or messages are verified by oracles or independent relayers.

characteristics.name: Validator guardian signing
characteristics.definition: Cross-chain messages are signed by a validator or guardian network.

characteristics.name: No cross-chain function
characteristics.definition: The object does not transfer assets or messages across blockchains.

dimensions.name: Price or rate determination
dimensions.definition: How the core service sets prices or interest rates.
dimensions.application_rule: Assign by the mechanism that sets prices or rates for the core service. Use external price feed for objects that deliver off-chain prices into smart contracts. Use the negation when the object sets no prices or rates.

characteristics.name: Pool-based pricing
characteristics.definition: Prices are set by a shared liquidity pool, either by following an automated market maker curve over pooled token reserves or by acting as the counterparty to traders.

characteristics.name: Order-book matching
characteristics.definition: Trades are matched in an order book.

characteristics.name: Algorithmic interest rate curve
characteristics.definition: Interest rates are set algorithmically from supply and demand or a strategy curve.

characteristics.name: External price feed
characteristics.definition: Off-chain prices and data are delivered into smart contracts.

characteristics.name: No price or rate setting
characteristics.definition: The object sets no prices or rates.

dimensions.name: Asset management approach
dimensions.definition: How DeFi asset management decides investments and trades: by a professional team, by users through smart contracts, or by an integrated platform combining both.
dimensions.application_rule: Observe who makes the investment decisions and executes trades for users. Choose active management when a professional team decides and trades; passive management when users create their own indices or structured products as smart contracts; integrated platform when both ways are combined. Use the negation when the object offers no asset management.

characteristics.name: Active asset management
characteristics.definition: A professional team makes investment decisions and trades.

characteristics.name: Passive asset management
characteristics.definition: Users create their own indices, structured products and more in the form of smart contracts.

characteristics.name: Integrated platform
characteristics.definition: The platform combines active and passive ways, offering quantitative analysis with machine learning.

characteristics.name: No asset management
characteristics.definition: The object offers no asset management service.

dimensions.name: Token standard
dimensions.definition: The fungibility standard of the main token used by the DeFi application, which determines its tailored use scenarios.
dimensions.application_rule: Identify the main token the application issues or uses for its core service and assign the standard that matches its fungibility: fungible for interchangeable currency, voting or pledge tokens; non-fungible for unique digital items; semi-fungible for tokens that mix both traits, such as gaming or copyright items. Use the negation when the object issues or uses no token.

characteristics.name: Fungible token standard
characteristics.definition: The token is fungible and interchangeable, as with the ERC-20 standard used for currencies, voting tokens and pledge tokens.

characteristics.name: Non-fungible token standard
characteristics.definition: The token is non-fungible, as with the ERC-721 standard used for artwork and digital collections.

characteristics.name: Semi-fungible token standard
characteristics.definition: The token is semi-fungible, as with the ERC-1155 standard used in GameFi and copyright.

characteristics.name: No token standard
characteristics.definition: The object issues or uses no token.

dimensions.name: Oracle architecture
dimensions.definition: The data source architecture of the oracles that deliver external data to the application's smart contracts.
dimensions.application_rule: Observe where the data used by the core service comes from: assign on-chain when data stays within the blockchain; off-chain when data comes from outside the blockchain; aggregated when on-chain and off-chain data or several off-chain sources are combined. Use the negation when the object uses no oracle.

characteristics.name: On-chain data
characteristics.definition: Data within a blockchain.

characteristics.name: Off-chain data
characteristics.definition: Data from outside a blockchain.

characteristics.name: Aggregated data
characteristics.definition: A combination of on-chain and off-chain data, or of different off-chain sources.

characteristics.name: No oracle
characteristics.definition: The object uses no oracle.

details.O1: 83 objects, 10 dimensions; 0 objects not classified in every dimension
details.O2: objects are registered once and never merged or split
details.O3: 0 characteristics without objects; conceptual or negation, exempt: D3.C3 'No token or member governance', D6.C3 'No cross-chain function', D8.C2 'Passive asset management', D8.C3 'Integrated platform', D9.C3 'Semi-fungible token standard', D9.C4 'No token standard', D10.C1 'On-chain data', D10.C4 'No oracle'
details.O5: not checked: only the e iterations after the first are checked
details.O7: no duplicate characteristic within a dimension

concise.justification: The taxonomy has ten dimensions across three perspectives, and each serves the stated purpose of classifying DeFi applications, analysing value propositions and supporting regulation. The sparsely populated dimensions are conceptual or technology-specific and do not add unnecessary complexity for these users.

robust.justification: The dimensions separate objects on meaningful criteria, and the D2 precedence rule and the merged D7 characteristic remove the overlaps raised earlier, so characteristics within each dimension are mutually exclusive. The skewed distributions reflect the evidence rather than a lack of differentiation.

comprehensive.justification: Every object can be placed through the negation characteristics, and all three perspectives (strategy, organization, technology) are represented by dimensions relevant to the purpose. The misfit shares reflect the evidence and do not show a missing characteristic.

extendible.justification: Each dimension is defined independently and includes a negation characteristic, so new characteristics or dimensions can be added within the existing perspectives without restructuring.

explanatory.justification: Each dimension and characteristic has a clear definition and application rule that ties it to the nature of DeFi applications and the stated purpose. The D2 precedence rule makes the stablecoin classification explicit.

evaluation_plan.users_aim: classify objects that represent a certain phenomenon
evaluation_plan.designers_provide: characteristics and dimensions that serve as scheme to classify one particular object

criteria.label: mean Cohen's kappa between the two classifications
share of new objects with a misfit in some dimension

evaluation_plan.users_aim: analyze objects that represent a certain phenomenon
evaluation_plan.designers_provide: characteristics and dimensions that serve as a basis to determine similarities and differences of objects
evaluation_plan.method: distribution of all classified objects over the characteristics

criteria.label: share of dimensions in which no characteristic holds more than the dominance threshold of the informed objects
